`umami-kotlin` is a Kotlin Multiplatform wrapper for the Umami web analytics REST API.

Modules: `:umami` (core), `:sample:simple-compose-app`, `:sample:terminalApp`. `:umami` packages: `api` (REST API), `core` (HTTP client/event queue), `domain` (models/value objects). Uses Ktor networking, Kotlinx Coroutines, Kotlinx Serialization, `kotlin.time.Instant`, Kermit, Kotest, Mokkery, and `Channel`-based producer-consumer event processing. `UmamiOptionsBuilder` uses the Builder pattern; `Umami` is a facade. Client engines vary by target (OkHttp Android/JVM, Darwin iOS).

All contributions must adhere to the guidelines outlined in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

Gradle project; recommended IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition or Android Studio. Detekt configuration: `detekt/detekt.yml`; Detekt runs automatically before a git push. Qlty configuration: `.qlty/qlty.toml`. Please ensure your changes do not introduce any new static analysis issues. Kover enforces coverage; requirements are in root `build.gradle.kts`.

All new features must be accompanied by tests. Bug fixes should also include a test that reproduces the bug. All new tests should use Kotest matchers (e.g., `shouldBe`) instead of `kotlin.test` assertions.

When verifying that your changes compile and work correctly, run the JVM tests for the specific module you modified. Using `jvmTest` ensures compatibility with environments that don't have the Android SDK installed:
```text
./gradlew :umami:jvmTest
./gradlew :umami-api:jvmTest
./gradlew :sample:terminalApp:jvmTest
```
Running tests will verify that the code compiles correctly, as compilation is a prerequisite for test execution. Full compilation and integration checks for all platforms (including Android) are performed automatically in the CI stage.

Dokka docs: `./gradlew dokkaHtml`. Publishing uses `maven-publish` to Maven Central. Update this document for significant architectural, major library, or build-process changes.

**Libraries/Frameworks:** NEVER assume a library/framework is available or appropriate. Ve
